name: Trotskyism
summary: Trotskyism is the family of Marxist currents descended from Leon Trotsky's Left Opposition and the Fourth International. Its branches share socialist revolution led by a workers' party, rule by elected workers' councils, expropriation and democratic planning of the key economy, internationalism against imperialism and nationalism, and rejection of Stalinism. They differ on the nature of the USSR and on unions, identity politics and other questions.
scope: Family entry: answers only what independent Trotskyist currents share. Branches read from their own programmes: the ICFI/SEP (orthodox, Statement of Principles), the USFI (Mandel, 1985 resolution), the Cliffite IST (ISO Where We Stand, Cliff), the Militant/CWI tradition (Socialist Party), Morenism (LIT history) and Cannon's SWP. Trotsky's 1930s writings are the common origin, not counted as a branch. Lambertism was sought but no programme text could be opened, so it is not used. Orthodox-trotskyism, shachtmanism and posadism have their own entries. Positions held by one branch only are null; opposed positions are 0, low.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The USFI rejects substitutionism, where a party acts in the class's name, the ISO says only mass struggle of workers can end capitalism, and the SEP stresses winning the working class.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: The SEP programme defends the basic right of people to resist the occupation of their country by foreign armies, and the ISO supports the self-determination of oppressed nations.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Cannon's testimony records the SWP's programme fighting anti-Semitism, and the SEP and Socialist Party oppose religious and racial discrimination.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The SEP says the imperialist drive for dominance leads inevitably to war, and the ISO, Socialist Party and LIT likewise tie war to capitalism and imperialism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The SEP says capitalism long ago exhausted its historically progressive role, implying it once had one, and the Socialist Party credits capitalism with the technology a socialist plan would use.

central-planning.rationale: The Socialist Party, SEP and USFI hold that democratically planned production beats the market, though the USFI warns that bureaucratic top-down planning is wasteful.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Socialist Party and SEP demand state and public provision of care, health, housing and benefits.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The ISO, SEP and Socialist Party oppose imperialism as the subjugation of weaker nations by stronger ones.

class-collaboration.rationale: The ISO, SEP and Socialist Party treat workers and employers as opposed classes and reject partnership, and the Socialist Party criticises class-collaborationist leaders.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The SEP and USFI treat class rule and class struggle as the structure of history, as feudalism gave way to capitalism and capitalism must give way to socialism.

colonial-socialism-democratic-stage.rationale: The SEP and LIT programmes follow Trotsky's theory of permanent revolution, in which the working class itself takes up the democratic tasks the bourgeoisie cannot fulfil, with no separate prior stage.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The ISO, SEP, Socialist Party and LIT oppose imperialism and colonial exploitation.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Socialist Party points to cronyism and corporate donations, the SEP to corporate and financial elite control, and the ISO to the corporate-dominated two-party system.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The SEP, ISO and Socialist Party demand an end to discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, which excludes criminalising it.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The Socialist Party demands living benefits for all who need them and the SEP demands guaranteed employment, medical care, education and housing; neither treats welfare as harmful.

defeat-communism.rationale: The branches are themselves communists or revolutionary Marxists who seek socialism, and they oppose imperialist anti-communist wars.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The USFI and orthodox programmes treat the nationalised property of the bureaucratised workers' states as something to defend, while the Cliffite programme calls those states state capitalist and opposes both blocs, so the branches' programmes point opposite ways.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The USFI resolution and LIT history adopt the dictatorship of the proletariat as workers' power, but the USFI insists it be democratic and restrict repression to violence, and the ISO and Socialist Party speak of a democratic workers' state.

direct-action.rationale: The Socialist Party and ISO stress mass working-class action and strikes but also stand candidates and build a workers' party for elections, so the branches combine both.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The SEP, ISO and Socialist Party oppose racism and racial discrimination in all forms.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The SEP, ISO and Socialist Party demand full legal, social and political equality for women and the end of gender discrimination.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The SEP, Socialist Party and USFI all treat climate change as a grave crisis demanding a socialist reorganisation, including nationalised energy and a switch to clean power, but they stress that capitalist governments will not do it.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Socialist Party calls for abolition of the monarchy and elected representatives, and the USFI bases power on democratically elected soviets.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The SEP demands full equality for all people and defends their democratic rights, and the ISO and Socialist Party likewise demand equality and an end to discrimination.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The USFI demands the presumption of innocence, public trials and a ban on torture, and the Socialist Party and SEP defend civil liberties.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Socialist Party, ISO and LIT back self-determination for nations including independence, which excludes military force to prevent it.

free-public-college.rationale: The Socialist Party demands free education with no tuition fees, the USFI lists free education among workers' democracy's tasks, and the SEP demands access to quality education.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The SEP, ISO and Socialist Party demand an end to discrimination on grounds of race, gender, sexuality and religion.

gradual-change.rationale: The SEP says capitalism is beyond reform, and the ISO says reforms within capitalism cannot end exploitation; the Socialist Party's transitional programme aims at a socialist break.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: The SEP programme attributes the global warming crisis to the profit system rather than to population growth or science, and the Socialist Party treats it as a capitalist failure.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The ISO and Socialist Party hold that profit comes from workers' labour and that wealth should go to those who produce it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Socialist Party says capitalist independence gives no escape and demands independent socialist nations, and the LIT's permanent revolution holds that democratic tasks need workers' power.

independent-unions.rationale: The Socialist Party and ISO want unions independent of the capitalist state and controlled by members, and the SEP condemns union leaders' integration with employers.

indirect-election.rationale: The USFI foresees pyramid soviets with delegates from lower councils, though it also supports referendums and direct democracy, and the ISO and LIT also base the state on councils of delegates.

informal-organisation.rationale: The SEP, ISO, USFI and LIT build disciplined revolutionary parties and mass workers' organisations rather than small informal groups.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Socialist Party demands the right to full-time work for all who want it, the SEP universal employment and the USFI the right to work.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The ISO says workers create society's wealth, and Cannon's testimony explains profit as surplus value from workers' labour.

leader-cult.rationale: The USFI condemns the arbitrary despotism and state religion of Stalin's type, the SEP blames the Stalinist dictatorial regime, and the ISO and Socialist Party condemn Stalinism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Socialist Party demands the NHS, water and public transport in public ownership, and the SEP and ISO put the key resources under collective control.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The SEP demands full citizenship rights for all immigrants, the ISO opposes immigration controls, and the Socialist Party demands the right to asylum.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The SEP, the USFI and the Socialist Party all replace the market's law of value with democratic economic planning, calling the market anarchic and the planned economy superior.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The SEP, USFI and ISO treat economic structure and class relations as the roots of political change.

material-over-identity.rationale: The SEP strongly opposes identity politics in favour of class unity, while the ISO and Socialist Party also back campaigns for the special oppressions, so the branches split.

nation-first.rationale: The SEP, ISO, Socialist Party and LIT all put international working-class unity above national interest and reject national programmes.

national-self-determination.rationale: The ISO and LIT support the right of oppressed nations to self-determination, and the Socialist Party supports the right of nations to self-determination within a voluntary socialist confederation.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The SEP defends peoples' right to defend themselves, and the USFI and Cannon accept defensive force by workers.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Every branch programme has the state own or control the economy through public ownership and planning, which a night-watchman state excludes.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: The USFI resolution places a transition period of workers' state between capitalism and socialism, with the state withering away from its start.

one-party-rule.rationale: The USFI resolution requires free competing soviet parties and rejects any vanguard monopoly, and the Socialist Party would give all parties media access in proportion to their vote.

open-borders.rationale: The SEP asserts the right of workers of every country to live and work where they choose and the ISO opposes all immigration controls; no branch states the opposite.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: The SEP programmes say socialist reorganisation cannot be carried out within the existing institutions of bourgeois democracy, and the ISO says the present state is built to protect capitalist rule and must be replaced by a workers' state.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Socialist Party wants mass participation in every aspect of decision-making in workplaces and communities, the USFI foresees self-administration by the toilers, and the ISO and LIT want councils of workers' delegates.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The LIT builds its organisation on democratic centralism and the Socialist Party stresses acting collectively on decided policy, though the USFI stresses wide rights of tendencies.

people-in-arms.rationale: The USFI calls for general armament of the proletariat and a drastic reduction of the permanent army, and Cannon advocates a state without a standing army or police opposed to the people.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Socialist Party and SEP oppose the capitalist EU yet both advocate a socialist union or United Socialist States of Europe, so they reject the EU while backing supranational unity on other terms.

population-transfer.rationale: The USFI rejects collective responsibility of social groups for individual acts, and the SEP opposes discrimination on national, ethnic and religious grounds.

positive-liberty.rationale: The USFI says bourgeois democratic rights are limited in practice by social inequality and that workers' democracy must guarantee material rights such as work, a secure existence and education.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Socialist Party calls the free press a myth owned by billionaires, and the USFI says social inequality restricts democratic freedoms in practice.

production-for-use.rationale: The SEP, ISO, Socialist Party and USFI all say production should be planned to meet human needs rather than profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The ISO says a minority class profits from the labour of the majority, and the SEP, Socialist Party and USFI likewise describe capitalism as exploitation of workers.

property-franchise.rationale: The USFI defends the universal franchise and the SEP, ISO and Socialist Party defend and extend democratic rights to the working class.

property-fundamental.rationale: Every branch programme calls for expropriating private ownership of the means of production, which cannot be squared with treating property as very hard to override.

public-ownership.rationale: The SEP programme transfers key industrial, financial and natural resources to society under workers' control, the Socialist Party demands nationalising energy, rail, water and the top 150 companies, and the ISO and USFI call for expropriating the capitalists.

racial-franchise.rationale: The SEP, ISO and Socialist Party demand equal rights and oppose racism, and the USFI defends universal franchise.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The SEP, ISO and Socialist Party oppose racism in all forms and demand an end to racial discrimination; Cannon's testimony cites the party's programme against race prejudice.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The ISO treats racism as a main division in the working class and Black liberation as key, and the Socialist Party says racism is built into capitalism.

recall-officials.rationale: The USFI resolution gives voters the right to recall delegates and judges at all times, and the Socialist Party demands instant recall of all MPs.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The SEP demands the unconditional right of workers of every country to live and work where they choose, the ISO opposes all immigration controls, and the Socialist Party opposes racist immigration laws.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The Socialist Party condemns the austerity forced on Greece by EU institutions and demands no cuts, and the LIT campaigned to stop foreign-debt payments.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The USFI resolution limits delegates' income to that of skilled workers and the Socialist Party demands a worker's wage for all representatives.

restore-past-order.rationale: The branch programmes aim at a socialist future and hold that capitalism must be replaced, not restored or preserved.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Socialist Party demands repeal of the anti-union laws and the right to strike, the ISO sees the strike as the workers' central power, and the USFI defends the right to organise unions.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: The SEP programme, the ISO statement and the USFI resolution all hold that the working class must overthrow capitalism by socialist revolution.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Socialist Party supports Scottish independence and the right of nations to self-determination, the ISO and LIT support self-determination of oppressed nations, and none opposes it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The USFI makes destroying the bourgeois state apparatus a prerequisite of workers' power, the ISO calls for an entirely different kind of state, and the Socialist Party says the capitalist state is not neutral.

social-market-economy.rationale: The SEP says capitalism is beyond reform, and the ISO and Socialist Party say reforms cannot end exploitation; they reject a regulated market as the settlement.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The ISO, USFI, SEP, Socialist Party and LIT make workers' own political power the test of socialism, and the Cliffite book denies socialism in Russia for the same reason.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The SEP, Socialist Party, ISO and USFI all hold that socialism cannot be completed or kept in one country, and the LIT and USFI base their programme on permanent revolution.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Cliffite current holds the USSR was state capitalist, while the USFI and the SEP describe a degenerated or bureaucratically betrayed workers' state, so the branches split though all say it was not socialism.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The USFI calls for general armament of the proletariat and abolition of any monopoly on weapons, and Cannon advocates workers' militias.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The SEP quotes Engels's definition of the state as an instrument of class rule, the USFI describes the state apparatus as serving class rule, and the Socialist Party and ISO say the capitalist state is not neutral.

state-harmful.rationale: Branches call for a workers' state based on councils and treat the state as a necessary instrument in the transition (the USFI says it should begin to wither away only gradually), not as unnecessary and harmful.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The USFI makes freedom of parties and tendencies a precondition of workers' democracy and rejects repressing opinion, and the Socialist Party would give every party media access.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The ISO, SEP, Socialist Party and LIT all oppose imperialism, meaning domination of weaker nations by stronger ones.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: The SEP programmes demand immediate withdrawal of US and British forces from Iraq and Afghanistan (the UK one also from all overseas bases), and the ISO opposes US intervention abroad.

unions-good.rationale: The Socialist Party and ISO programmes support unions as essential, while the SEP statement blames the union bureaucracies for betraying and weakening workers, so the branches split.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The British Socialist Party programme demands a free, publicly run NHS, the SEP programme demands unrestricted access to quality medical care, and the USFI resolution lists a secure existence and social rights among workers' democracy's tasks.

vanguard-party.rationale: The SEP, ISO, USFI, LIT and Socialist Party all hold that a revolutionary party is needed to bring socialist consciousness to the working class and lead it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Socialist Party speaks of the dictatorship of billionaire owners over the media, the USFI says inequality restricts democratic freedoms, and the SEP sees corporate and financial elite rule.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The ISO says women's liberation is impossible without socialist revolution, and the Socialist Party and USFI treat women's oppression as rooted in class society.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The SEP, ISO and Socialist Party demand full legal and social equality for women.

women-suffrage.rationale: The USFI defends universal franchise as a right won by struggle, and the SEP and ISO demand full political equality for women.

worker-ownership.rationale: The ISO programme speaks of workers collectively owning and controlling the wealth, though the Socialist Party and SEP express this as public ownership under workers' control rather than firm-by-firm ownership.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: The SEP rejects alliances that make workers sacrifice their independent interests (the Popular Front), and the ISO calls for political independence from capitalist parties.

workers-councils.rationale: The USFI resolution, the ISO programme and the LIT history all make elected workers' councils (soviets) the basis of state power, and the Socialist Party calls for decision-making bodies of workplace and community delegates.

workers-nation.rationale: The SEP, ISO, Socialist Party and LIT insist the working class organise and fight internationally.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Socialist Party calls for a new mass workers' party, the ISO for independence from the two capitalist parties, and the SEP for the political independence of the working class.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Socialist Party demands democratic workers' control and management of nationalised industry, the SEP puts key resources under democratic supervision of the working class, and the ISO and LIT also call for workers' control.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The USFI and LIT describe the exploitation and plundering of semi-colonial countries by imperialism.

notes: Only the SEP/ICFI, USFI, Cliffite, CWI and Morenoist programmes were read in full or in part; Lambertism could not be sourced. Many statements stay null because the branch programmes are silent. The Socialist Party text is the 2023 What We Stand For document; the Bristol page (s7) is an older copy of CWI demands used for cross-checking. SEP (ICFI) attitude to unions and identity politics opposes the other branches, hence the 0 answers. Pass of 2026-11-23: all eleven sources re-saved (s6 converted from its .docx); sources tagged words (programmes and scholarship; no Trotskyist party held state power); 121 new statements answered, 8 from the programmes, the rest null.
